subject: DPA: vendor list cadence & objection window
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@fargoanalytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@fargoanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: DPA / subprocessors: preferred notification cadence and objection window

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. As we move toward finalizing the DPA, our legal ops team asked for two clarifications before we sign: a consistent cadence for providing the subprocessor list (snapshot vs. rolling), and the objection window length for newly added subprocessors.

Our baseline language is: 45 days' notice for new subprocessors, with a quarterly consolidated snapshot and ad hoc notifications for critical changes. Could you confirm Redwood’s standard practice and whether you can accept 45 days? If not, please propose the alternative and any restrictions (e.g., carve-outs for infra providers, emergency security patching).

Also attaching the version of the DPA with our call-outs for quick reference.

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Fargo Analytics
legalops@fargoanalytics.com

Attachment: dpa_fargo_redline_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@fargoanalytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA / subprocessors: preferred notification cadence and objection window

Sara — thanks for the clear note and for sharing the redlines. Looping in our contracts and security leads to propose a concrete path forward.

High-level proposal from Redwood:
- Notification cadence: quarterly consolidated snapshot (CSV) plus immediate notice for any change that we deem critical (security, export control, or changes that impact processing locations).
- Objection window: 30 days for standard additions; 45 days if the prospective processor requires custom onboarding that could materially change risk posture.
- Carve-outs: emergency remediation vendors (e.g., incident response retained firms) will be notified as soon as feasible but will be treated as exceptions to the regular notice window.

We can accommodate Fargo’s preference for a 45-day window in contract if we put a pragmatic exception list (incident response, CDN edge infra, short-term pilots). Laura, Rishi — can you confirm draft contract language and redline constraints? Kar, can you confirm this aligns with the commercial timeline?

Evelyn Hart
Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: vendor_list_snapshot_20261204.csv (csv)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@fargoanalytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T11:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA / subprocessors: preferred notification cadence and objection window

Sara, Evelyn — quick read from Contracts:

1) We can accept a 30-day standard objection period. To give Fargo comfort, we will add an escalation path that effectively pauses onboarding if a substantive objection is raised within the period (we treat requests as in good faith).

2) We propose the following contract language for the subprocessor clause:
   - Redwood will provide a quarterly snapshot of subprocessors and will notify the Controller of new subprocessors no fewer than 30 days prior to permitting access to Processor systems.
   - For any new subprocessor that Redwood reasonably designates as a "material-risk subprocessor", Redwood will provide 45 days' notice and cooperate on reasonable mitigation steps if the Controller objects.
   - Emergency remediation vendors are exempted from the advance notice requirement; Redwood will notify Controller promptly after engagement.

3) We will include a mutual-acknowledgement DocuSign flow: Fargo to confirm receipt of the snapshot; Redwood to confirm remediation timelines if an objection escalates.

I will attach a redline with this language — please review and tell me if Fargo needs the 45-day window to be unconditional.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: draft_subprocessor_clause_redline.docx (docx)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: DPA / subprocessors: preferred notification cadence and objection window

Sara — appreciate the straightforward asks. From a go-live/commercial standpoint, Redwood prefers the 30-day standard with the 45-day material-risk carve-out Laura suggested. That lets us keep onboarding timelines tight while giving Fargo contractual protections for higher-risk vendors.

Operationally: we will run the first quarterly snapshot on 2027-01-01 and include a rolling CSV export for the next 60 days to help Fargo reconcile during the initial cutover.

If Fargo is comfortable with those terms, we can send the final DPA via DocuSign by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Kar (Karthik Iyer)
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
